comparison.description: Voyager 1 in August 2012 and Voyager 2 in November 2018 are separate historical observations, not simultaneous boundary samples. Their positions do not establish a global heliopause surface.

crossings.name: Voyager 1 heliopause crossing

geometry.physical_uncertainty: Not supplied for this interval. These are sampled numerical interpolation residuals, not physical orbit uncertainty or continuous error bounds.

crossings.epoch_note: 12:00 UTC represents the published crossing date for navigation; it is not a measured crossing time. The plotted vector is the admitted mission prediction, not an observed 3-D coordinate or a vector rescaled to 121.6 AU.
crossings.interpretation: A persistent rise in galactic cosmic rays and decrease in heliospheric particles marked the transition. Plasma-wave observations subsequently established the denser interstellar environment; Voyager 1's direct plasma instrument was no longer operating.

crossings.name: Voyager 2 heliopause crossing

geometry.physical_uncertainty: Not supplied for this interval. These are sampled numerical interpolation residuals, not physical orbit uncertainty or continuous error bounds.

crossings.epoch_note: 12:00 UTC represents the published crossing date for navigation; it is not a measured crossing time. The plotted vector is the admitted mission prediction, not an observed 3-D coordinate or a vector rescaled to 119 AU.
crossings.interpretation: The working plasma instrument measured the transition from hot, tenuous solar-wind plasma to colder, denser local interstellar plasma, supported by particle observations.

components.name: Solar wind
components.description: The Sun supplies a flowing plasma. Any visible particles illustrate the concept; they are not measured individual paths or visible-light emission.

components.name: Termination shock
components.description: The supersonic solar wind slows to subsonic flow. Voyager encountered this shock at different dates and distances: about 94 AU in December 2004 and 84 AU in August 2007.

components.name: Heliosheath
components.description: The region of slowed and heated solar-wind plasma between the termination shock and heliopause.

components.name: Heliopause
components.description: The transition between solar-wind plasma and local interstellar plasma. It is neither a visible solid wall nor the limit of the Sun's gravity.

components.name: Local interstellar medium
components.description: Plasma, neutral atoms and magnetic fields surround the heliosphere. Interstellar space begins long before the theoretical outer extent of the gravitational Solar System.

model_literature.title: Opher et al. — pickup-ion MHD model (2020)
model_literature.assumptions: Treats pickup ions separately from thermal solar-wind ions; charge exchange with neutral hydrogen removes energy. The model uses an interstellar magnetic-field orientation constrained by the IBEX Ribbon and predicts a more compact, lobed heliosphere.
model_literature.limitations: A particular physical model, not a uniquely measured surface. This application has not qualified its numerical output grid, boundary conditions, solver reproduction or redistribution rights; no mesh here reproduces this model.

model_literature.title: Kleimann et al. — large-scale heliosphere model comparison (2022)
model_literature.assumptions: Reviews analytical, MHD, multifluid and kinetic treatments. Solar-wind pressure and solar-cycle history, interstellar plasma and magnetic field, neutral-hydrogen exchange, and tail mixing affect the predicted boundaries and large-scale tail.
model_literature.limitations: Long-tailed and compact or lobed geometries differ with assumptions and treatment of the heliopause. ENA observations constrain models through an additional emission and transport calculation; angular brightness is not distance. The article's CC BY 4.0 license does not by itself qualify a numerical source grid.

limitations: Transparent layers are a conceptual teaching diagram. Their dimensions and shape are artistic parameters, not fitted global boundaries or a reproduced published model.
The historical Voyager vectors and observed crossing radii are separate anchors; they are never forced onto a modeled shell.

The heliosphere changes with solar-wind conditions and the surrounding medium. No qualified time-dependent boundary model is supplied, so the conceptual scene does not claim current-epoch boundary motion.
An exact published scientific heliosphere reconstruction remains incomplete. IBEX angular ENA maps do not uniquely determine a 3-D heliopause.
These broad NASA explanatory ranges describe uncertain theoretical extents, not measured inner or outer surfaces.

The Oort Cloud has not been directly observed as a complete population. Sparse markers illustrate a hypothesized reservoir; they have no catalog identities, measured positions or calibrated number density.
The heliopause marks a plasma transition, not the Sun's gravitational limit. The Oort Cloud is hypothesized far beyond it.
Long-period comet observations motivate the reservoir hypothesis. An observed comet orbit does not measure or map the entire source population.

comet_examples.name: C/2012 S1 (ISON)
comet_examples.description: NASA discusses ISON as an Oort Cloud comet; it disintegrated during its 2013 passage near the Sun. This context entry does not add an orbit or a measured reservoir location.

comet_examples.name: C/2013 A1 (Siding Spring)
comet_examples.description: NASA identifies Siding Spring as an Oort Cloud example that passed Mars in 2014. No source-qualified orbit has been added for this example.
